sources.name: In-house QC Laboratory
sources.description: The company's own quality-control laboratory. Uses validated, ICH-compliant methods; full 24/7 instrument logs retained.

sources.name: StabilTech Vendor Services
sources.description: External vendor providing stability-chamber hosting and outsourced assay services. Contracted since 2023.

sources.name: Process Engineering Group

sources.name: External Literature and Quoted Studies
sources.description: Published and preprint studies, conference abstracts, and quoted third-party analyses referenced during the audit.

artifacts.title: Bioavailability Study — RX-441 vs Reference (Phase I, n=24)
artifacts.content: Randomized, open-label, single-dose, two-period crossover study in 24 healthy volunteers (powered to detect a 10% difference at 80% power, alpha 0.05). Primary endpoint AUC0-inf. RX-441 geometric mean AUC = 12,450 ng*h/mL; reference = 10,820 ng*h/mL. Geometric mean ratio (RX-441/reference) = 1.15, 90% CI 1.08-1.22, i.e. a 15% increase in bioavailability. The 90% CI for the ratio excludes 1.40. No safety signals. Conclusion: the new formulation increases bioavailability by approximately 15%, not 40%.

artifacts.title: Reference Formulation Baseline AUC (pooled)
artifacts.content: Reference formulation AUC0-inf from three prior bioequivalence studies (n=24 each): 10,780; 10,850; 10,810 ng*h/mL. Pooled geometric mean = 10,813 ng*h/mL. This is the established baseline against which RX-441 is compared.

artifacts.title: Stability Study — 25C/60% RH, 6 Months (validated ICH method)
artifacts.content: Accelerated stability study per ICH Q1A(R2), 25C/60% RH, 6 months. Degradation products quantified by a VALIDATED HPLC method (validation report QC-VAL-221: linearity r2=0.9998, accuracy 99.2-100.8%, precision RSD<1.5%). Degradation product D-2 at 6 months: 0.18% (below the 0.5% acceptance threshold). Potency: 99.1% (within 98-102% spec). Conclusion: RX-441 is chemically stable at 25C/60% RH over 6 months.

artifacts.title: Controlled Temperature-Effect Study (batch age held constant)
artifacts.content: To test whether storage temperature causes potency loss, all batches were matched to the same age (3 months old) before a further 3-month storage at 5C, 25C, or 40C. Potency loss after the additional 3 months: 0.4% (5C), 0.5% (25C), 0.6% (40C). One-way ANOVA: temperature effect not statistically significant (p=0.71). Conclusion: with batch age held constant, storage temperature does NOT significantly drive potency loss.

artifacts.title: QC Batch Assay Logs — new granulation process (12 batches)
artifacts.content: Assay (% of label claim) for 12 consecutive batches produced with the new granulation process. Reported batch-to-batch CV (assay) = 3.1%. All 12 batches within 98-102% spec. No out-of-spec results.

artifacts.title: In-house stability chamber 24/7 validated log (6 months)
artifacts.content: Continuous 24/7 temperature/RH logging for the in-house stability chamber, sensor calibrated per ISO 17025 (calibration certificate CAL-118, uncertainty +/-0.3C). Over 6 months: 2 temperature excursions (both <1C, duration <30 min, auto-recovered). Total logged hours: 4,380 (full coverage, no gaps).

artifacts.title: Lab-scale potency report (RX-441, 5 lab batches)
artifacts.content: Lab-scale (10 L) production of RX-441, 5 batches. Potency by validated HPLC: 99.2, 99.6, 99.8, 99.4, 99.7 (%). Mean potency = 99.5% (SD 0.2%). All within 98-102% spec.

artifacts.title: StabilTech stability report — D-2 at 0.7% (6 months)
artifacts.content: StabilTech outsourced stability assay of RX-441 at 25C/60% RH, 6 months. Reports degradation product D-2 = 0.7% (above the 0.5% acceptance threshold) and recommends the product be considered unstable. Method: in-house HPLC method ST-HPLC-7. Note: ST-HPLC-7 has NOT undergone formal method validation (no linearity, accuracy, or precision validation on file); StabilTech states the method is 'in routine use'.

artifacts.title: StabilTech chamber reliability report — '99.9% uptime'
artifacts.content: StabilTech reports its stability chamber achieved '99.9% uptime' over 6 months and concludes it is more reliable than typical in-house chambers. Methodology note: uptime was computed from sensor readings collected only during business hours (08:00-18:00, Mon-Fri); readings outside this window were excluded from the calculation. The chamber's primary temperature sensor was found to be out of calibration (drift +1.8C) during the period and was not recalibrated until month 5.

artifacts.title: StabilTech 'independent confirmation' of bioavailability gain
artifacts.content: StabilTech offers an 'independent confirmation' that RX-441 increases bioavailability by 40%. Basis: a re-analysis of a 6-subject pilot dataset (n=6, single dose, no reference-period washout verification, no confidence interval reported). StabilTech describes the result as 'definitive confirmation of a 40% gain'. No additional subjects were enrolled and no powered study was conducted.

artifacts.title: Granulation process comparison report (old vs new)
artifacts.content: Process engineering comparison of the old and new granulation processes, each run for 12 consecutive batches. Batch-to-batch CV (assay): old process = 8.2%, new process = 3.1%. The new process reduces batch-to-batch variability by more than half. Change control CC-2041 approved the new process.

artifacts.title: Old granulation process batch logs (12 batches, baseline)
artifacts.content: Assay (% of label claim) for 12 consecutive batches produced with the OLD granulation process (pre-change baseline). Reported batch-to-batch CV (assay) = 8.2%. Three of 12 batches required rework to reach spec.

artifacts.title: Manufacturing cost analysis — '25% reduction'
artifacts.content: Process engineering cost model for the new RX-441 formulation. Headline: '25% manufacturing cost reduction vs current process.' The model attributes the FULL annual cost of the solvent-recovery line ($1.2M) to RX-441 under the old process and $0 under the new process. Note: the solvent-recovery line is SHARED with two other products and its cost is allocated across all three; the model does not apply the standard allocation factor.

artifacts.title: Pilot-scale batch logs (RX-441, 3 pilot batches)
artifacts.content: Pilot-scale (200 L) production of RX-441, 3 batches. Potency by validated HPLC: 98.9, 100.4, 99.8 (%). Mean potency = 99.7% (range 98.9-100.4%). All within 98-102% spec.

artifacts.title: Quoted study: 'RX-441 shows 40% bioavailability gain' (n=6 pilot)
artifacts.content: A preprint (open access, not peer-reviewed) reports: 'The new RX-441 formulation showed a 40% increase in bioavailability relative to reference (n=6, p<0.05).' The study enrolled 6 subjects, reports a single point estimate with NO confidence interval, and the authors state the result is 'definitive'. The preprint's own limitations section notes the sample size was 'underpowered for precise estimation'.

artifacts.title: Quoted study: temperature-potency correlation (r=0.85)
artifacts.content: A conference abstract reports a strong correlation between storage temperature and potency loss across archived RX-441 batches (Pearson r=0.85, p<0.01) and concludes 'higher storage temperature causes potency loss.' The abstract does not control for batch age; the archived batches stored at higher temperature were also, on average, the OLDER batches (mean age 9 months vs 4 months for cooler-stored batches). No randomized or age-matched design was used.

artifacts.title: Quoted study: granulation and content uniformity in similar APIs
artifacts.content: A peer-reviewed study of three structurally similar oral APIs reports that switching to a controlled granulation process reduced batch-to-batch assay CV from a mean of 7.9% to 3.4% (p<0.01, n=15 batches per process). The authors conclude controlled granulation is an effective lever for reducing content-uniformity variability.

artifacts.title: Quoted guidance: allocating shared overhead in product cost models
artifacts.content: A peer-reviewed cost-accounting paper on pharmaceutical manufacturing states: 'Shared utility and recovery infrastructure must be allocated across all products that use it, using a documented allocation factor; attributing 100% of a shared asset's cost to a single product systematically overstates that product's cost and any apparent cost reduction from changing it.'
